name: Endometrial Carcinoma (Bokhman Classification, Lynch Syndrome, FIGO Staging)

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / FIGO Committee on Gynecologic Oncology
clinicalPearls: Postmenopausal bleeding is the presenting symptom in over ninety percent of women with endometrial carcinoma
Transvaginal ultrasound endometrial thickness above four millimeters in postmenopausal women mandates histological sampling
Bokhman Type I endometrioid carcinoma is estrogen-dependent arising from hyperplasia, harboring PTEN mutations
Bokhman Type II serous or clear cell carcinoma is estrogen-independent, aggressive, and characterized by TP53 mutations
Lynch syndrome mismatch repair deficiency confers a forty to sixty percent lifetime risk of endometrial cancer
reference.pathophysiology: Endometrial carcinoma develops along two distinct pathogenic pathways. Type I endometrioid tumors arise from prolonged unopposed estrogen stimulation (obesity, nulliparity, tamoxifen) causing atypical hyperplasia with PTEN, PIK3CA, and mismatch repair defects. Type II serous tumors arise in atrophic endometrium of elderly women from p53-mutated endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma (EIC), behaving aggressively with early transtubal peritoneal dissemination.
additionalDifferentials: Endometrial atrophy (most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding)
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal ultrasound measurement of endometrial stripe thickness
Pipelle outpatient endometrial biopsy or hysteroscopic D&C
Pelvic MRI for depth of myometrial invasion and cervical stromal extension
Universal immunohistochemistry screening for mismatch repair proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2)
